items.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995
items.q: I was working in a place called Monroe’s Uptown House and we had two trumpet players: Vic Coulson and Joe Treadwell

ctx.x: Yeah. And if you don’t like it you don’t have to listen to it.

So well yeah, but I found out you have to listen to find out what they’re doing. And it’s new so it’s strange, so you have to get used to — give it a good listen and find out what they’re doing. I know the first time I heard bop well I’d been around Dizzy quite a bit, so he was just getting it together, you know with the flat fives and raised ninths. And nobody knew what he was doing. He used to drive little trumpet players crazy. I was working in a place called Monroe’s Uptown House and we had two trumpet…
Wasn’t that the place where Thelonious Monk was doing some of that early —
